claims.text: Sulfur ion implantation followed by controlled annealing will induce an in situ layered dichalcogenide sulfide film on CoCrFeMnNi.
The sulfur implantation and annealing treatment will reduce both friction coefficient and wear rate over a broad temperature range.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is homogeneous and single-phase FCC.
Annealing will facilitate implanted-sulfur diffusion and reaction with alloy elements.
The treatment will remain effective from approximately 77 K to 800 °C.
A controlled or inert atmosphere minimizes uncontrolled oxidation during tribological service.
The treatment forms a continuous nano-layered sulfide film having a dichalcogenide structure.
The proposed sulfide film can self-adapt and self-heal during sliding.
Implanted sulfur diffuses to the near-surface region during annealing and forms a layered sulfide phase by reacting with CoCrFeMnNi constituents.
Weak interlayer bonding in layered two-dimensional materials enables low interfacial shear.
A low-shear layered film reduces friction and wear by limiting direct metal-to-metal contact.
The treated alloy will have a friction coefficient below 0.15.
The treated alloy will have at least a tenfold lower wear rate than the untreated alloy.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi can exhibit a friction coefficient of approximately 0.3 under inert or ultra-high-vacuum sliding conditions.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi typically has higher wear rates under sliding conditions comparable to the proposed tests.
The lubricating effect will persist only while the controlled atmosphere is maintained and the sulfide film remains uncontaminated and mechanically intact.
Extreme mechanical loads exceeding design limits will disrupt the film or its lubricating effectiveness.
MoS2 and related two-dimensional materials have demonstrated strong solid-lubrication behavior associated with weak interlayer interactions.
The long-term stability and self-healing capability of the proposed sulfide film under cyclic sliding and varying humidity remain unvalidated.
